\[
I_{\text{out}} =
\begin{cases}
\operatorname{mean}\,\{\, w \in W : |w - z| \le k\sigma \,\} & \text{if at least } K \text{ values are in range} \\
\operatorname{mean}\,(N_8) & \text{otherwise}
\end{cases}
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(z\): The center value
- \(k\sigma\): The half-width of the accepted range
- \(K\): The minimum count
- \(N_8\): The eight neighbors of the center

z is the center value and W the window. Only values within k sigma of z take part in the mean. Values across an edge differ from z by more than that, so they are left out, and the edge stays. If fewer than K values, the minimum count, are in range, z is an isolated spot of noise, and the output is the mean of its eight neighbors N_8.
